narrative.overview:
Every download is a parcel a bot mails to the user, and the window is the post-office counter where it is addressed, sent and collected. The world is airmail stationery: pale blue airmail paper as the ground, a deep post-office blue shell bar, airmail red reserved for the act of sending and for alarm, white panels ruled with fine blue-grey lines. It is a working desk, not a dashboard and not a website: dense, quiet, with the postal devices (stamp, postmark, waybill, chevron border) carrying the identity so the data does not have to.

Two voices share the work. A condensed postal-label face (Barlow Condensed, uppercase, tracked) speaks for labels, column heads, stamps and the one big number; a sober grotesk (Public Sans) carries every datum. Numerals are tabular everywhere, so sizes, counts and percentages stand in columns. The log and the pasted request are the only places that drop into monospace, because they are the protocol showing through on demand.

Depth is almost flat: two white panels lift a hair off the paper, and the only motion with character is the postmark landing on the envelope when the transfer changes state.
keyCharacteristics: Airmail palette: post blue shell, airmail red action, blue-grey rules on pale blue paper.
Condensed uppercase postal labels over a plain grotesk for data; tabular numerals throughout.
Dense table rows (36px) and compact 40px controls; one 6px radius family.
Signature devices: the red/white/blue chevron progress strip and the rotated circular postmark.
Fonts bundled locally (strict CSP); light scheme only.

rules.name: The Red Means Send Rule
rules.body: Airmail red is the act of sending (search button, progress chevron) or an alarm (error, invalid input). It never decorates a neutral control and never appears as a second primary button.

rules.name: The Status Has a Datum Rule
rules.body: A state colour never stands alone: every state badge sits beside the file name or message it describes, and the postmark repeats network, date and state in words.

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body; numeric columns align right. Never switch it off for a figure.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Condensed uppercase names things; the grotesk states values. A datum (file name, bot, path, size) is never set in the condensed label face.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Inside a panel, hierarchy comes from 1px rules, letterhead tint and type, never from cards with shadows.

dos: Do keep airmail red for sending and alarms only; the primary download action is post blue.
Do set labels, column heads and stamps in Barlow Condensed uppercase with 0.06-0.08em tracking, and every value in Public Sans.
Do keep tabular numerals and right-aligned numeric columns; table rows stay at 36px.
Do pair every state colour with words: badge plus message, postmark with network, date and state.
Do separate content inside panels with 1px blue-grey rules and the letterhead tint.
Do bundle any new font locally; the CSP allows nothing external.
Do honour reduced motion: no postmark stamp, no strip or button transitions.
donts: Don't use a solid single-colour progress bar; progress is the airmail chevron, proportional to bytes.
Don't add shadows to elements inside a panel; only the two desk panels are lifted.
Don't set file names, paths or other data in the condensed label face or in uppercase.
Don't introduce a dark terminal look for the log or the request; they stay light, in a letterhead well.
Don't loosen table density to make room; drop a column through the container query instead.
